types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information to the executor.

types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByURL`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.description: An issue is a work item owned by a team, with a title and a status in that team’s workflow. Use projects to group related work, cycles to plan when to work on it, and parent issues to organize sub-issues. The UUID stays the same when an issue moves between teams; its human-readable identifier changes.

fields.description: The resource's unique UUID. This stays unchanged when the resource is renamed or moved; use it for stored references and mutations.
fields.name: id

fields.description: The resource’s recorded creation time, in UTC. Imports may preserve an earlier creation time.
fields.name: createdAt

fields.description: When the resource was last meaningfully updated, in UTC. Some background or housekeeping changes do not advance this timestamp.
fields.name: updatedAt

fields.description: When the resource was archived, in UTC. Null while active, including after unarchiving. Archived resources still exist but are normally excluded from lists unless `includeArchived` is true.
fields.name: archivedAt

fields.description: The issue’s number within its current team. Combine it with the team key to form an identifier such as ENG-123, or read the identifier field directly. Numbers are not necessarily consecutive.
fields.name: number

fields.description: The issue title.
fields.name: title

fields.description: The priority of the issue. 0 = No priority, 1 = Urgent, 2 = High, 3 = Medium, 4 = Low.
fields.name: priority

fields.description: The numeric estimate in the team’s configured scale. For T-shirt estimates, the stored values 1, 2, 3, 5, and 8 correspond to XS through XL, with 13 and 21 for extended sizes. Zero is an explicit estimate; null means the issue has not been estimated.
fields.name: estimate

fields.description: The order of the item in its column on the board.
fields.name: boardOrder

fields.description: The issue’s position in manually sorted lists, with lower values first. Use a value between two neighboring issues to place it between them; Linear may adjust positions to avoid collisions.
fields.name: sortOrder

fields.description: The issue’s position within its priority group, with lower values first. This order is separate from sortOrder, which is used for other manually sorted lists.
fields.name: prioritySortOrder

fields.description: Time the issue entered a started status. Cleared when moved back to triage, backlog, or an unstarted status.
fields.name: startedAt

fields.description: Time the issue entered a completed status. Null when it is not completed.
fields.name: completedAt

fields.description: Time the issue most recently entered triage. Null if it has never entered triage.
fields.name: startedTriageAt

fields.description: Time the issue last left triage. Null before triage is completed or after re-entering triage.
fields.name: triagedAt

fields.description: Time the issue entered a canceled or duplicate status. Cleared when it leaves those status types.
fields.name: canceledAt

fields.description: The time the issue was automatically closed after inactivity. Null if it has not been auto-closed or its status has changed since then.
fields.name: autoClosedAt

fields.description: The time the issue was automatically archived under the team’s inactivity settings. Null if it was not auto-archived or has since been restored.
fields.name: autoArchivedAt

fields.description: Due date in YYYY-MM-DD format, without a time or time zone. Null if no due date is set.
fields.name: dueDate

fields.description: Time the current SLA started. Null if no SLA is set.
fields.name: slaStartedAt

fields.description: Time the current SLA enters medium risk. Null if no SLA is set.
fields.name: slaMediumRiskAt

fields.description: Time the current SLA enters high risk. Null if no SLA is set.
fields.name: slaHighRiskAt

fields.description: Deadline after which the current SLA is breached. Null if no SLA is set.
fields.name: slaBreachesAt

fields.description: How SLA days are counted: all for calendar days, or onlyBusinessDays for the team’s working days.
fields.name: slaType

fields.description: The time the issue was added to its current project. Changes when the project changes, and is null when the issue has no project.
fields.name: addedToProjectAt

fields.description: The time the issue was added to its current cycle. Changes when the cycle changes, and is null when the issue has no cycle.
fields.name: addedToCycleAt

fields.description: The time the issue was created in or moved to its current team. Use this to distinguish a team move from the issue’s original creation time.
fields.name: addedToTeamAt

fields.description: Whether the issue is in the trash: true for a trashed issue, null otherwise. Trashed issues are also archived and are scheduled for permanent deletion after the grace period.
fields.name: trashed

fields.description: Time until which the issue is hidden from triage. Null if it is not snoozed.
fields.name: snoozedUntilAt

fields.description: The UUIDs of labels assigned to the issue. Use labels to read their names, colors, and groups, or use these IDs when comparing or updating label assignments.
fields.name: labelIds

fields.description: The team that owns the issue. Its settings determine the available statuses, estimation scale, and cycle schedule.
fields.name: team

fields.description: The cycle that the issue is associated with. Null if the issue is not part of any cycle.
fields.name: cycle

fields.description: The project that the issue is associated with. Null if the issue is not part of any project.
fields.name: project

fields.description: Milestone within the issue’s project. Null if no milestone is assigned.
fields.name: projectMilestone

fields.description: The most recently applied issue template. This records where the issue’s defaults came from; subsequent edits to the template do not replace the issue’s current values. Null if no template is recorded or it was deleted.
fields.name: lastAppliedTemplate

fields.description: The recurring template that created the issue. Null if none is recorded or the template was deleted.
fields.name: recurringIssueTemplate

fields.description: Identifiers the issue used before it moved between teams. Use identifier for its current identifier and id for a UUID that remains stable across team moves.
fields.name: previousIdentifiers

fields.description: The user who created the issue. Null if the creator's account has been deleted or if the issue was created by an integration or system process.
fields.name: creator

fields.description: The external user who created the issue. Set when the issue was created via an integration (e.g., Slack, Intercom) on behalf of a non-Linear user. Null if the issue was created by a Linear user.
fields.name: externalUserCreator

fields.description: The user to whom the issue is assigned. Null if the issue is unassigned.
fields.name: assignee

fields.description: The agent delegated to work on the issue. Null if no agent is delegated.
fields.name: delegate

fields.description: The user who last snoozed the issue in triage. Null if no snoozing user is recorded, the snooze was cleared, or the user was deleted.
fields.name: snoozedBy

fields.description: The issue’s current status in its team’s workflow. The status name is customizable; its type identifies the workflow category, such as started or completed.
fields.name: state

fields.description: The issue’s position among its parent’s direct sub-issues, with lower values first. Null for top-level issues. This order is independent of the issue’s position in team lists.
fields.name: subIssueSortOrder

fields.description: Emoji reaction summary for the issue, grouped by emoji type. Contains the count and reacting user information for each emoji.
fields.name: reactionData

fields.description: Display name for priority: No priority, Urgent, High, Medium, or Low.
fields.name: priorityLabel

fields.description: The comment from which this issue was created. Null if none is recorded or the comment was deleted.
fields.name: sourceComment

fields.description: The integration service recorded as the source of this issue. Null when no integration source is recorded; this does not indicate whether the issue is currently syncing with an external service.
fields.name: integrationSourceType

fields.description: Whether this issue inherits shared access from its parent issue.
fields.name: inheritsSharedAccess

args.description: The data used for email authentication.

fields.description: Starts email sign-in and sends a one-time token to the supplied address. Generate and retain a clientAuthCode UUID, then pass it with the emailed token to emailTokenUserAccountAuth within ten minutes. Requesting another challenge replaces the stored client binding for that email. When login challenge verification is enabled, challengeResponse is also required. Success confirms the challenge was accepted; email delivery may finish in the background.

Successful authentication consumes the client binding and sets a session cookie. Use the returned memberships and available or locked workspaces to continue into a workspace; the deprecated token field is not populated. An expired token or a code from a different client cannot complete this flow.
fields.name: emailTokenUserAccountAuth

args.description: The data used for token authentication.
args.name: input

fields.description: Completes SAML sign-in with the email and token issued by the SAML flow, then sets the authentication cookie. The response identifies workspace memberships and any workspaces that require a different sign-in method. Unlike email token sign-in, this operation does not require clientAuthCode.
fields.name: samlTokenUserAccountAuth

types.description: A Linear comment thread associated with an external conversation, issue, or message. Use url to open the source when a link is available, isConnected to check the retained sync relation, and the personal-integration fields to determine whether the current user needs to connect an account before replying. These fields describe stored connection state, not a live delivery test.

fields.description: The external source ID, or the email message ID for email threads. Null when unavailable.
fields.name: id

fields.description: The source category, such as integration. subType identifies the external service.
fields.name: type

fields.description: The specific integration service for the external source (e.g., 'slack', 'jira', 'github', 'salesforce'). Null if the source type does not have a sub-type.
fields.name: subType

fields.description: A human-readable display name for the external source (e.g., 'Slack', 'Jira', 'GitHub').
fields.name: name

fields.description: A human-readable display name for the thread, derived from the external source. For Slack threads this is the channel name, for Jira it's the issue key, for email it's the sender name and count of other participants.
fields.name: displayName

fields.description: A URL linking to the thread in the external service. For example, a Slack message permalink, a Jira issue URL, or a GitHub issue URL.
fields.name: url

fields.description: Whether the thread retains its external connection and has not been explicitly disconnected. This does not guarantee that comment delivery succeeds.
fields.name: isConnected

fields.description: Whether the current user has a working personal integration connected for the external service. For example, whether they have connected their personal Jira, GitHub, or Slack account. A connected personal integration may still return false if it has an authentication error.
fields.name: isPersonalIntegrationConnected

fields.description: Whether a connected personal integration is required to post comments in this synced thread. True for Jira and GitHub threads, where comments must be attributed to a specific user in the external system. False for Slack and other services where the workspace integration can post on behalf of users.
fields.name: isPersonalIntegrationRequired

fields.description: The resource’s recorded creation time, in UTC. Imports may preserve an earlier creation time.

fields.description: When the resource was last meaningfully updated, in UTC. Some background or housekeeping changes do not advance this timestamp.

fields.description: The team's name.
fields.name: name

fields.description: The team's unique key, used as a prefix in issue identifiers (e.g., 'ENG' in 'ENG-123') and in URLs.

fields.name: description

fields.description: The icon of the team.
fields.name: icon

fields.description: The team's color.

fields.description: The workspace that the team belongs to.
fields.name: organization

fields.description: The team directly above this one in the hierarchy. A sub-team can inherit settings and resources from its parent. Null for a top-level team.
fields.name: parent

fields.description: Whether the team plans work in cycles.
fields.name: cyclesEnabled

fields.description: The day of the week that a new cycle starts (0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday, ..., 6 = Saturday).
fields.name: cycleStartDay

fields.description: The length of each cycle, in weeks. Together with cycleCooldownTime, this determines the repeating cycle schedule.
fields.name: cycleDuration

fields.name: cycleCooldownTime

fields.description: Whether starting an issue automatically adds it to the current cycle.
fields.name: cycleIssueAutoAssignStarted

fields.description: Whether completing an issue automatically adds it to the current cycle.
fields.name: cycleIssueAutoAssignCompleted

fields.description: Auto assign issues to current cycle if in active status.
fields.name: cycleLockToActive

fields.description: How many upcoming cycles to create.
fields.name: upcomingCycleCount

fields.description: The IANA time zone used for team schedules, such as Europe/Helsinki. Defaults to America/Los_Angeles.
fields.name: timezone

fields.description: Whether the team should inherit its workflow statuses from its parent. Only applies to sub-teams.
fields.name: inheritWorkflowStatuses

fields.description: Whether the team should inherit its estimation settings from its parent. Only applies to sub-teams.
fields.name: inheritIssueEstimation

fields.description: The issue estimation type to use. Must be one of "notUsed", "exponential", "fibonacci", "linear", "tShirt".
fields.name: issueEstimationType

fields.description: [DEPRECATED] Whether issues without priority should be sorted first.
fields.name: issueOrderingNoPriorityFirst

fields.description: Whether to allow zeros in issues estimates.
fields.name: issueEstimationAllowZero

fields.description: Where an issue is placed after a status change: first, last, or noAction to keep its position.
fields.name: setIssueSortOrderOnStateChange

fields.description: Whether to add additional points to the estimate scale.
fields.name: issueEstimationExtended

fields.description: The estimate used in progress calculations for issues without an explicit estimate. A value of 1 makes unestimated issues contribute to scope; 0 excludes their weight from estimate-based totals.
fields.name: defaultIssueEstimate

fields.description: Whether triage mode is enabled for the team. When enabled, issues created by non-members or integrations are routed to a triage state for review before entering the normal workflow.

fields.description: The default workflow state into which issues are set when they are opened by team members.

fields.description: The id of the default template to use for new issues created by members of the team.

fields.description: The default issue template for users who are not members of this team. Null if no non-member template is configured.

fields.description: The workflow state into which issues are set when they are opened by non-team members or integrations if triage is enabled.
fields.name: triageIssueState

fields.description: Whether the team is private. Private teams are only visible to their members and require an explicit invitation to join.
fields.name: private

fields.description: Whether all members in the workspace can join the team. Only used for public teams.
fields.name: allMembersCanJoin

fields.description: Security settings for the team, including role-based restrictions for issue sharing, label management, member management, template management, and agent skills.

fields.description: Whether the team is managed by a SCIM integration. SCIM-managed teams have their membership controlled by the identity provider.

fields.description: The SCIM group name for the team.

fields.description: The workflow state into which issues are moved when a PR has been opened as draft.

fields.description: The workflow state into which issues are moved when a PR has been opened.
fields.name: startWorkflowState

fields.description: The workflow state into which issues are moved when a review has been requested for the PR.
fields.name: reviewWorkflowState

fields.description: The workflow state into which issues are moved when a PR is ready to be merged.
fields.name: mergeableWorkflowState

fields.description: The workflow state into which issues are moved when a PR has been merged.
fields.name: mergeWorkflowState

fields.description: Whether to group recent issue history entries.
fields.name: groupIssueHistory

fields.description: Whether to enable resolved thread AI summaries.
fields.name: aiThreadSummariesEnabled

fields.description: Whether to enable AI discussion summaries for issues in this team.
fields.name: aiDiscussionSummariesEnabled

fields.description: Whether to send new issue notifications to Slack.
fields.name: slackNewIssue

fields.description: Whether to send new issue comment notifications to Slack.
fields.name: slackIssueComments

fields.description: Whether to send new issue status updates to Slack.
fields.name: slackIssueStatuses

fields.description: Period after which issues are automatically closed in months. Null/undefined means disabled.
fields.name: autoClosePeriod

fields.description: The canceled workflow state which auto closed issues will be set to. Defaults to the first canceled state.
fields.name: autoCloseStateId

fields.description: Months after which closed issues are automatically archived: 1, 3, 6, 9, or 12.
fields.name: autoArchivePeriod

fields.description: Whether parent issues should automatically close when all child issues are closed
fields.name: autoCloseParentIssues

fields.description: Whether child issues should automatically close when their parent issue is closed
fields.name: autoCloseChildIssues

fields.description: Calendar feed URL (iCal) for cycles.
fields.name: cycleCalenderUrl

fields.description: The visibility of the team. Returns public for teams visible to all workspace members, private for teams visible only to members, and restricted for non-private teams inside a private-team boundary.
